name: Engineering Resilient Cognitive Systems
description:
The future of Artificial Intelligence is no longer taking place only on screens, but in our physical reality. Physical AI and Embodied Intelligence are the key technologies for the world of tomorrow – from life-saving medical products to intelligent robotics and autonomous driving.

But with this power comes great responsibility: How can we ensure that these learning systems do not become an unacceptable risk to humans?

Become a shaper of responsible AI and learn in this lecture how to not just apply Machine Learning, but how to do so safely and valuably for society. The reason why we still do not have widespread autonomous mobility today, for example, is not a lack of AI models – it is the missing proof of their safety.

Become an expert on the question: How do we engineer resilient cognitive systems that people can entrust their lives to?

Your Roadmap for Physical AI & Safety Engineering:

1. Resilience as a Foundation: Learn how we engineer cognitive systems that work safely and yet with maximum performance even in unpredictable situations.

2. Safety Engineering: Learn that safety is much more than fulfilling standards. Learn how we create innovations and progress that we can entrust our lives to.

3. Safe AI: Get to know the specific challenges of AI and dive into the current state of research on how to assure safety of AI-based systems.

4. Adaptive Intelligence: Learn how systems can adapt autonomously to guarantee safety and maximum benefit despite unpredictable environments.

Why you should attend this lecture: 
You will get the unique chance to combine deep technical competence with societal relevance. You will learn how to not just apply AI, but how to develop AI-based systems in a way that they safely improve our future – an essential skill building block for your career.

Flexible learning – shaping together: 
The lecture will be recorded and made available online. However, the true experience takes place in the lecture hall: On-site, we complement the theory with interactive discussions and practical elements where we directly put the concepts to the test together.
